gaps: Pool ceiling configuration (pool_max) was not verified: the query_metric call for it was refused with budget_exhausted (ev_10).
Request rate was not checked, so it is unknown whether the trigger was a load surge or connection leakage.
CPU and memory usage of the service process were not queried; only event-loop utilization was available.
Error patterns over the baseline window returned empty (ev_13), so baseline error content could not be compared beyond what was inferred from the empty result.
A follow-up log search was cut off by budget exhaustion (ev_14).
No logs from other services or dependency-side logs (e.g. the database server) were checked for concurrent issues.
report.summary: demo-service hit its database connection-pool ceiling: connections in use climbed to the pool limit, requests began queueing for a connection, and pool wait times grew past the client timeout, producing connection-timeout errors, a 5xx error-ratio breach and a p95 latency spike. Event-loop utilization and database operation latency stayed flat throughout, so the service was waiting on pool acquisition rather than being CPU-bound or slowed by the database.

timeline.event: Pool connections in use begin climbing after sitting at zero at the start of the window.
Pool queue forms: pending requests jump and pool wait p95 rises sharply while pool usage reaches its ceiling.
First "timeout exceeded when trying to connect" error is logged.
HTTP p95 latency jumps to {lat_at_2557} s and the 5xx error ratio to {er_at_2557}.
Peak impact: p95 latency {lat_max} s, 5xx ratio {er_max}, pool wait p95 {pw_max} s.
Detection rules http-latency-p95 and http-error-ratio fire.

hypotheses.statement: Connection-pool exhaustion in demo-service caused the incident: connections in use reached {pu_max}, pending acquisition requests reached {pp_max} with pool wait p95 of {pw_max} s, and the resulting connection timeouts drove p95 latency to {lat_max} s and the 5xx ratio to {er_max}.
Slowness in a downstream dependency caused the latency spike and 5xx errors.
CPU/event-loop saturation within demo-service caused the latency spike and errors.

observations.statement: Pool connections in use rose from {pu_first} at the start of the window to a maximum of {pu_max} connections at {pu_max_at}, and stayed there through the end of the window.
Requests pending on the pool were {pp_at_2542} at 20:25:42 and peaked at {pp_max} requests at {pp_max_at}, from {pp_first} earlier in the window.
Pool wait p95 rose from {pw_first} s in the early window to {pw_at_2542} s at 20:25:42 and {pw_max} s at {pw_max_at}.
HTTP p95 latency was flat for the window and the preceding baseline (baseline max {lat_base} s), then jumped to {lat_at_2557} s at 20:25:57 and {lat_max} s at {lat_max_at}.
The 5xx error ratio was {er_early} up to and including the sample at 20:25:42, then reached {er_at_2557} at 20:25:57 and {er_max} at 20:26:12.

The dominant error pattern in the incident window is "request failed" with exception "timeout exceeded when trying to connect", {ep_count} occurrences from 20:25:56.202Z to 20:26:13.404Z, all on service version 1.0.1.
Error log volume was {err_at_2600} lines in the 20:26:00 minute, while warn lines totalled {warn_sum} over the whole window.
Event-loop utilization stayed low throughout the window, peaking at {elu_max} and sitting at {elu_at_2542} at 20:25:42 when the pool queue formed.
Database operation p95 latency stayed flat, between {db_min} s and {db_max} s, across the whole incident window.
Loki search in the window returns only 409 "order rejected" warnings on route /orders ({l1_status} for every returned line), spread across service versions 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 from 20:24:01.886Z onwards.

recommendations.action: Verify the configured pool maximum and raise it (or shard the pool) so that the observed {pp_max} queued requests at peak load can be served without hitting the ceiling.
recommendations.rationale: Pool in-use connections saturated at {pu_max} while {pp_max} requests queued and pool wait p95 reached {pw_max} s, indicating the pool size is the binding constraint.

recommendations.action: Instrument and alert on pool_pending > 0 and pool_wait_p95 crossing the request timeout as leading indicators, ahead of p95 latency and error-ratio SLO thresholds.
recommendations.rationale: Queue formation and wait-time growth led the latency and 5xx breach by roughly one scrape interval, so pool metrics give earlier warning.

recommendations.action: Audit connection acquisition/release paths for connections not returned to the pool, and review query timeouts and request-level connection handling.
recommendations.rationale: Connections rising to the ceiling plus queueing with flat DB operation latency suggests acquisition pressure; leaks or long-held connections have not been checked.

recommendations.action: Run a full latency breakdown of downstream dependencies (not just DB operation p95) to confirm none contributed to the queue formation.
recommendations.rationale: Dependency slowness remains a low-confidence alternative; only DB operation p95 was measured as flat.

recommendations.action: Review CPU and event-loop metrics under peak load to confirm the process is not CPU-bound during the pool-queue periods.
recommendations.rationale: Event-loop utilization stayed low, so CPU saturation is unlikely, but the process's CPU usage was not directly examined.
